root.name: Lion Defense: Anti-Philidor
root.moves: 1. e4 d6 2. d4 Nf6 3. Nc3 Nbd7 4. f4

overview: White plays 4.f4 against the Lion, taking space with e4, d4 and f4 in an Austrian-Attack style set-up. Black answers 4...e5, the Lion's Cave, aiming at the d4 centre; after 5.Nf3 exd4 6.Qxd4 c6 White gets a lead in development and Black a solid shell. The game is open and lively, with White's pawn centre as the target and Black's pieces ready to strike back.

white_ideas.idea: Take space with e4, d4, f4 and develop Nf3 and Bd3
Maintain the centre or recapture on d4 with the queen

typical_structures.structure: Philidor-style structure with Black d6/e5 and White f4/e4

character.notes: Both sides have real chances of tactics; the f4/e5 clash makes it double-edged.

gambit.notes: No material changes in the main line.

structure.notes: Central pawn exchanges give open lines.

approach.notes: Played by strong players now and then, but not a main line.

level.notes: Plans against the f4 centre are subtle.

sublines_that_differ.name: Lion Claw Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 d6 2. d4 Nf6 3. Nc3 Nbd7 4. f4 e5 5. Nf3 exd4 6. Qxd4 c6 7. Bc4 d5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black gambits a pawn for open lines and quick development.

character.reason: The f4 centre against ...e5 invites tactics and double-edged play.

gambit.reason: The main line is not a gambit; Lion Claw is a sub-line.

structure.reason: Pawns are exchanged on d4, opening the position.

approach.reason: The Lion is respectable but rare; the Pirc relation is mainstream.

level.reason: Theory is limited but needs good understanding.

plans.reason: No named plan is clearly characteristic.
